alignments.note: Waw takes and (rule 14).
Verb takes subject, auxiliary and lexical verb (rule 17).
Verb takes subject, auxiliary, lexical verb and the phrasal particle up, which leaves the head on the verb (rule 44).
עַל rendered to.
Construct noun with no article morpheme in the chain takes the supplied the (rule 29).

Rectum takes of + noun (rule 19); the two English words render the one substantive, headed on villages, which already names the thing, with unwalled as its specifier (rule 31, as with sea monsters). The margin's an open country is noted but the text is followed.
Verb takes subject, auxiliary and lexical verb; the to that reaches its bare object belongs to the verb's rendering, since no marker or preposition stands on that object (rule 44).
Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun and relative them that, headed on the pronoun (rule 41).
Participle keeps its own English with the supplied copula (rules 20, 41), headed on the lexeme-bearing rest.
Articleless participle recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied that with itself (rules 41, 46).
לָבֶטַח fuses to the single word securely under rule 30, headed on the noun.
Construct כֹּל takes only all (rule 19).
Suffix takes of them, headed on the pronoun.
Participle rendered dwelling.

בְּאֵין is rendered by the single word without, so the preposition and the existential particle share one unit under rule 30's one-English-word condition, headed on the negation (rule 48's closing sentence, for מֵאֵין → without).
Noun rendered walls.
Waw takes and.
Noun rendered bars.
Correlative neither ... nor: a present negative stands in the clause and takes the opening neither, so this waw takes only the closing nor (rule 14).
Noun rendered gates.
Existential אַיִן takes the negation word neither and heads on it (rules 14, 50).
The possessive לְ of a verbless clause carries the recast having (rule 43).
The ASV writes no subject pronoun for this suffix in the having neither ... nor recasting (rule 22).

review_notes: The neither/nor pair is split under rule 14: the present אֵין takes neither and the second waw takes nor.
The to at t018 is given to אָבוֹא's unit under rule 44, since the Hebrew object הַשֹּׁקְטִים carries no marker or preposition of its own.
